Project a hib, mixed-effects model

Source: R/hib_project_model.R
hib_project_model.Rd

This function projects a fitted hib model using the supplied model object and data to be used in projection - i.e., a dataframe/tibble or raster stack of covariates

Usage

hib_project_model(
  mod_obj,
  data,
  backtransform = NULL,
  rescale_specs = NULL,
  lme4_specs = NULL,
  inla_specs = NULL,
  brms_specs = NULL,
  calc_aoa = FALSE,
  cv_obj = NULL
)

Arguments

mod_obj

One of; HibModelLME4, HibModelINLA or HibModelBRMS.

data

Either a dataframe-like object or a raster stack that can be used to project onto - should contain x and y columns if a dataframe.

backtransform

A function that will backtransform the model response to the scale of the original variable, e.g., exp() as the inverse of log()

rescale_specs

A list containing details relevant to rescaling projections. Specifically, named items should consist of 'rescale' (logical), 'baseline_covar' (data.frame, or NULL), 'baseline_re_form' (formula, NA, or NULL). In combination, these arguments determine if predictions will be rescaled or not (based on value of $rescale), the covariate values used to generate the baseline against which other predictions are rescaled ($baseline_covar), and whether/how random effects should be incorporated in the generation of this baseline ($baseline_re_form, see lme4/inla/brms_specs). If $rescale == TRUE, but no baseline_covar is provided, the intercept of the model will be used as the baseline value.

lme4_specs

A list containing details relevant to projecting an lme4-style model. Specifically, named items should consist of 'bootstrap' (logical) and 'n_boot' (numeric), indicating whether bootstrapped prediction intervals should be estimated, and if so, how many bootstrap samples should be used. In addition, 'calc_se' (logical) is used to specify whether or not a standard error based uncertainty estimate (via marginaleffects) is calculated and used to generate confidence intervals. 'conf_level' (numeric) is used to specify the confidence levels of intervals generated via bootstrapping or the se-based approach. Values should fall between 0 and 1, typically in the range 0.5 to 0.95. Additionally, 're_form', as 're.form' in predict.merMod(), used to specify random effects to condition on when predicting an lme4 model (formula, NULL, or NA).

inla_specs

A list containing details relevant to projecting an inla-style model. 're_form', as 're.form' in predict.merMod(), used to specify random effects to condition on when predicting an inla model (formula, NULL, or NA). 'link_inverse' a function that is the invers of the link used to fit the model. Used to backtranform the global intercept for use in rescaling predictions.

brms_specs

A list containing details relevant to projecting a brms-style model. Specifically, named item should consist of 'incl_obs_uncert' (logical) to determine whether or not observation-level uncertainty is included in predictions. Setting this parameter to TRUE will produce predictions with larger uncertainty, using predict.brmsfit(), setting to FALSE calls fitted.brmsfit() internally. 'conf_level' (numeric) is used to specify the confidence levels of intervals generated. Values should fall between 0 and 1, typically in the range 0.5 to 0.95, internally converted to quantiles and passed to the probs argument of predict.brmsfit()/ fitted.brmsfit(). Additionally, 're_form', as 're_formula' in predict.brmsfit(), used to specify random effects to condition on when predicting a brms (formula, NULL, or NA).

calc_aoa

A logical to indicate whether or non the 'Area-of-applicability' (AOA) should be estimated - following Meyer and Pebesma (2021)

cv_obj

A HibCV object, used in AOA estimation.

Details

Expects a HibModel object and data for use in a projection.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
  proj <- hib_mod_project(hib_model, proj_data)
} # }
